paragraphs.anchor: And the lot of the children of Joseph.

paragraphs.text: On the north of Canaan, as Judah’s had fallen on the south: that these two strongest tribes might be as bulwarks to both sides of the kingdom. So in their march through the wilderness, in their several companies or brigades, God put a strong tribe to two weak tribes, as Judah to Issachar and Zebulon, &c. See Isa 26:1; Isa 40:11.
Afterwards made no less famous than wholesome by Elisha’s healing of them. {2Ki 2:21}
Hushai’s country, {2Sa 16:16} ennobled by his name, as Co was to Hippocrates, and little Hippo by great Augustine.
Where the Canaanites held them till Solomon’s days; but were then slain by Pharaoh, king of Egypt, in favour of his daughter, Solomon’s wife. {1Ki 9:16}

And it was a happiness to both that they lay together: but a shameful thing that afterwards it should be said, "Manasseh against Ephraim, and Ephraim against Manasseh; and they together against Judah." {Isa 9:21}
paragraphs.anchor: Manasseh and Ephraim took their inheritance.

paragraphs.text: As there were two Bethhorons, so Eusebius telleth us that there were two Ataroths: one near Rama; the other, four miles distant from Samaria.
paragraphs.anchor: Was Atarothaddar unto Bethhoron the upper.

paragraphs.text: Or, Westward by Michmethah, and then eastward by several towns here mentioned. These are ancient things, and to us hard to be understood.
i.e., To the territories, but not to the town itself, for that was part of Benjamin’s lot. {Jos 18:21}
So called from the plenty of apples that grew there: as Perton in Worcestershire is from the plenty of pears.
paragraphs.anchor: The border went out from Tappuah.

paragraphs.text: Allotted to Ephraim, a numerous tribe, within the portion of Manasseh.
Which is nothing for their commendation; but discovereth either their cowardice or covetousness, or both.
{See Trapp on "Jos 16:3"} They would not yield: so that Pharaoh was forced to fire their town. {1Ki 9:16}
